Kitch never published a public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or status page was ever published on kitch.io, and none appears in the Internet Archive's record of the domain. The kitch.io domain registration has since lapsed and now resolves to an unrelated third-party gambling site, so no live link is carried in this profile.

providers.name: Local Kitchens
providers.description: Local Kitchens is a restaurant company that operates multi-brand "food hall" locations where a single kitchen prepares menu items from a curated set of local and national restaurant brands for on-demand pickup and delivery, ordered through its consumer website and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, it is a consumer-facing hospitality and food-ordering business. As of this pass it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation — its web presence is a Cloudflare-fronted marketing and ordering site (Google Workspace email, Klaviyo, Twilio, Zoom in its DNS records).

providers.name: Milano Vice
providers.description: Milano Vice is a Berlin-based virtual restaurant company founded in 2021 by Rudolf Donauer and Dennis Murselovic (both ex-Delivery Hero) that operates a digitally-powered, delivery-first pizza brand. It partners with professional kitchens across German cities including Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg and Frankfurt to prepare and deliver handmade pizzas and pinsa to homes and offices, orderable through its own website and third-party delivery platforms such as Lieferando, Wolt and Uber Eats. It is a consumer food brand backed by Speedinvest, Coefficient Capital, True and Geschwister Oetker, and does not currently publish a public developer API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Nextbite
providers.description: Nextbite is a virtual-restaurant / ghost-kitchen company that operates delivery-only food brands out of existing restaurant kitchens, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It reaches consumers through third-party delivery marketplaces rather than a public developer platform; its sister restaurant-ordering-aggregation product Ordermark has since merged into UrbanPiper (a DoorDash Preferred Integrations Partner). As of this enrichment pass Nextbite publishes only a thin marketing website (nextbite.com, "We Put Food on The Table") and exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: OneKitchen
providers.description: OneKitchen is a Dubai-based cloud/ghost-kitchen enablement startup founded in 2018 that provided chefs, restaurants, and food entrepreneurs with shared kitchen space, equipment, and operating technology to launch delivery-only restaurant brands in about 48 hours at a fraction of traditional restaurant capital cost. It was backed by 500 Global, Chernovetskyi Investment Group, and Savour Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company appears dormant - its primary domain joinonekitchen.com no longer resolves to a live product (it now redirects to a domain-sale parking page) and no public developer portal, API, documentation, or other API surface could be found.

providers.name: plated
providers.description: Plated was a meal-kit delivery company surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company was acquired by Albertsons in 2017 and later wound down; the plated.com domain now 301-redirects to safeway.com, and no independent developer portal, API reference, SDK, or well-known surface remains. This profile records the honest state of a defunct provider with no active API surface.

providers.name: Skipthedishes
providers.description: SkipTheDishes is a Canadian online food-delivery marketplace headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, founded in 2012 and acquired by Just Eat (now Just Eat Takeaway.com) in 2016, under which it operates as the group's Canadian brand. It connects diners with local restaurants and a network of independent couriers for on-demand food delivery and pickup across Canadian cities via its consumer website and mobile apps, and runs a restaurant partner onboarding program and a courier (Skip Network) program. As of this enrichment pass SkipTheDishes publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. The primary domain is served behind Cloudflare bot protection and the partner/partners subdomains are static marketing/onboarding pages, so no OpenAPI, webhook, or SDK surface is available to harvest.

providers.name: SpoonRocket
providers.description: SpoonRocket was an on-demand, prepared-meal delivery startup backed by a16z that delivered low-cost ready-to-eat meals on demand. The company has since ceased operations and its spoonrocket.com domain no longer resolves to a live website (AWS Route53 nameservers remain delegated, but there is no A record). It publishes no developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or public API surface. This profile remains in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead with no active API to enrich.

providers.name: Sweetgreen
providers.description: Sweetgreen is a fast-casual restaurant company (NYSE: SG) building healthy, plant-forward food through a network of company-owned locations and its digital ordering platform. It reaches customers primarily via its consumer website and mobile app for pickup, delivery, and its Sweetgreen Rewards loyalty program, and operates automated "Infinite Kitchen" locations. As of this enrichment pass, Sweetgreen publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture only. Backed by D1 Capital and True Ventures.

providers.name: TastyUrban
providers.description: TastyUrban is a Berlin-based virtual restaurant franchise and digital-first food-brand licensing company founded in 2022 by Felix Chrobog, Marc Hansell, and Gerry Pidgeon (alumni of Gorillas, Tier, and Deliveroo). It pursues an asset-light model in which existing restaurants and retail partners license and operate TastyUrban's digital food brands, using otherwise idle kitchen capacity to add revenue without major investment or operational complexity. The company is backed by Earlybird and raised a EUR 1.5M seed round in 2023 and a EUR 6.5M Series A in 2025 (led by IBB Ventures). TastyUrban operates a consumer/partner web presence at tastyurban.com but publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Yassir
providers.description: Yassir is an Algerian-founded super app providing on-demand and financial services across the Maghreb, sub-Saharan Africa, Canada, and France. Founded in 2017 by Noureddine Tayebi and headquartered in Palo Alto, California with operations centered in Algiers, the company bundles ride-hailing (Yassir Ride), food delivery (Yassir Food), grocery delivery (Yassir Market), and digital financial services (Yassir Cash) into a single consumer mobile app, alongside a Yassir B2B suite covering corporate mobility, meal benefits, procurement, parcel delivery, and digital gift cards. Yassir reports more than six million users, 130,000+ driver and merchant partners, and 4,500 employees operating across cities in Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, South Africa, Senegal, Canada, and France. The company has raised roughly $193M to date, including a $150M Series B led by BOND with participation from Y Combinator and DN Capital, and a global sponsorship partnership with Paris Saint-Germain. Yassir is a consumer and merchant-facing super app: it operates iOS and Android apps and a business portal (go-business.yassir.com) but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source project. Driver, courier, restaurant, and store onboarding flow through partner sign-up forms rather than a developer program, and the yassir-tech GitHub organization currently has no public repositories.

providers.name: Noon
providers.description: Noon is a Dubai-headquartered e-commerce marketplace and digital ecosystem launched in 2017 as a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Emirati businessman Mohamed Alabbar. Frequently described as the Amazon of the MENA region, Noon operates as the leading online shopping destination across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Egypt, offering electronics, mobiles, fashion, beauty, home, appliances, baby, and grocery categories through a hybrid first-party and third-party seller marketplace. Beyond the core marketplace, Noon has expanded into a lifestyle super-app spanning Noon Food (quick-service restaurant delivery competing with Talabat and Deliveroo), Noon Daily (next-day grocery delivery), Noon Minutes (15-minute instant grocery and essentials delivery), Noon Pay and the Noon mobile wallet (QR payments, bill pay, and a co-branded credit card), Noon VIP (loyalty/subscription), NowNow (on-demand delivery in KSA), and SIVVI (acquired regional fashion brand). Noon operates its own last-mile logistics arm and warehouses across the region, and provides a Fulfilled by Partner Integration (FBPI) program with commercial APIs that allow third-party sellers and channel-integration partners (ChannelEngine, Unicommerce, Vinculum, Ecom Energize and others) to programmatically publish catalog, sync inventory, and manage shipments. These APIs are gated to onboarded sellers and certified integrators inside the noon.partners environment — there is no general public developer portal, no published OpenAPI specification, and no Noon-maintained SDKs, CLIs, or open-source repositories.

providers.name: Swoop
providers.description: Swoop (formerly Thumo) is an African super-app building toward a single consumer platform for everyday commerce, starting with same-day food delivery and online shopping in Lagos, Nigeria (Yaba, Surulere, Gbagada and surrounding areas) and Eswatini, where it launched in 2025 and became the country's largest ecommerce platform. The app offers real-time order tracking, transparent upfront pricing, in-app support, and payments via card, bank transfer and OPay, with plans to add a payments app and further services on the road to a pan-African super-app. Founded by Thiel Fellow Aubrey Niederhoffer and Edwin Ruiz, Swoop raised a $7.3M seed round in 2026 with participation from Version One Ventures, Long Journey, Variant, Soma Capital and Dune. Swoop is a consumer-facing mobile and web platform; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation. This profile was surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Prosus Ventures
providers.description: Prosus Ventures is the venture-capital arm of Prosus, the Amsterdam-headquartered global consumer-internet and technology group (part of the Naspers group), founded in 2015 to make early-stage and growth-stage technology investments in high-growth markets outside the United States and China. The firm invests to "fuel the ecommerce flywheel," backing companies across food delivery, fintech, consumer services, logistics, e-commerce and marketplaces, plus a strong and growing focus on early-stage AI startups that reshape the e-commerce value chain (shopping and advertising tech, customer support, AI agents and operations) and frontier technologies such as quantum computing, robotics, space and biotech. Prosus Ventures typically invests from seed through Series B and into growth rounds, with a primary geographic focus on India, Latin America and Europe, plus activity in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and ANZ. In fiscal year 2025 the group committed and invested over $400 million across 40+ closed transactions, including roughly $88 million into AI. Its public portfolio spans 80+ companies including Meesho, Urban Company, PharmEasy, Klar, ElasticRun, BandLab, Ema, Corti and Oxford Ionics. The venture team is led by CEO Martin Tschopp with regional heads across India, Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
